text:
Filip Hallander is a 26-year-old Swedish center who came over from the Pittsburgh system and has played 11 games as an Oilers depth forward. He has three points, but none in his last ten games, and our numbers say that's not just luck: the chances have thinned out too. His ice time has dropped by about three minutes a night over that stretch, to around 10.

The puzzle is the on-ice numbers. Edmonton has taken 59% of the expected goals with him on the ice, about 11 points better than without him, which suggests the shifts are going fine even if he isn't the one producing. In 11 games, that can mean a lot of things, including good linemates and easy matchups.

Evolving-Hockey had too little of him last season to say much, 171 minutes, with opponents creating more chances against him in that sample. Our range for a full season is wide, 6 to 15 goals. With Ryan Nugent-Hopkins' status uncertain and Isaac Howard out, there may be minutes available down the middle. He needs a point or two to earn them.
headline: Hallander needs a point to earn minutes
